verdict_reason: An allow-listed agy reader can hide a command under a data-shaped key and stay usable, a --rev brief can be recorded under a hash the worktree did not get, and patch-claim cleanup can delete or replace another run's file.
reply_markdown:
## Q1
Byte hashes, not timestamps, decide a bound-input change (`orchestrate/mod.rs:446`; tree content at `revision.rs:409`). This run's patch is written before `collab_before` (`orchestrate/mod.rs:4055`) and only that file plus its temp name is exempt (`reviewed.rs:1503`). A sibling's other patch is a warning on a worktree and on muse, grok, claude and http; a complete live-tree agy reply with no writing step stays usable. A failed re-read is treated as a change: an empty hash or `missing` fails the reply (`orchestrate/mod.rs:446`). Codex in a worktree is exempt (`tree.rs:345`).

## Q2
The merge keeps both conflicting values (`agy.rs:470`). On an allow-listed reader only a Scanned string is tested (`tree_check.rs:241`). A key ending in `path`, `file`, `url`, `uri` or `dir` (and the other suffixes), or containing `query`, `pattern`, `regex`, `search`, `glob`, `include` or `exclude`, is data (`tree_check.rs:265`). Values such as `exec_path` = `rm -rf x`, `paths` = `bash -c rm`, `research` = `git clean -fd` (`research` contains `search`) and `global` = `rm -rf x` (`global` contains `glob`) are not writing. Any other tool name still counts as writing, so a complete agy reply is kept.

## Q3
Equal bytes share one content-addressed name. A crash after the synced temp and before publish leaves the temp, not a half-written final name. Without hard links the name is an empty claim, then a rename (`reviewed.rs:1268`); an empty file unchanged for 60s is taken over (`reviewed.rs:1188`). `drop_own_claim` and the takeover stat the file, then `remove_file` by name (`reviewed.rs:1232`, `reviewed.rs:1412`). A sibling that finishes in that gap is deleted. A live owner stalled past 60s can lose the claim and, where rename replaces, overwrite the other run, so the ledger sha256 is not the file. Excluded paths use a new index in the system temp directory (`reviewed.rs:1033`) via `GIT_INDEX_FILE` (`reviewed.rs:752`) and `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`. I saw no write to the repository index. A kill leaves that temp index in the temp directory.

## Q4
Without `--diff-tracked-only`, a one-revision patch still contains every untracked, not-ignored file (`reviewed.rs:978`). Gitignore and `.c3ignore` stay out. At most ten names are printed; a backtick or a control character is only counted (`reviewed.rs:1544`) while its bytes stay in the patch. The flag is on the CLI, detach (`detach.rs:220`) and panel members (`panel/run.rs:2290`, `member.rs:250`). MCP `c3_consult` forwards `diff` and has no flag (`mcp/mod.rs:318`, `mcp/mod.rs:971`).

## Q5
One start-of-run HEAD resolve is `rev_live_head` (`orchestrate/mod.rs:2725`). It withholds priors and is the handoff and ledger live HEAD, or unresolved when empty. Finding `source.base_commit` is the worktree fingerprint (`ledger.rs:51`). A later HEAD move does not change that launch value. A missing brief is hashed by `committed_brief`, which prefers the literal HEAD (`worktree.rs:934`). Staging reads again (`reviewed.rs:435`); drift skips the re-hash when `brief_from_revision` is set (`orchestrate/mod.rs:443`). The handoff can cite HEAD and a sha256 the worktree does not hold.

## Q6
`explain` elects with `skip_preflight` and `no_network` (`cli/router.rs:264`), reads records and searches PATH, and I saw no child process and no consultation write. Replay reads sessions only. Any invalid `ext.c3.draw` row, including a missing `mult`, drops the whole block (`replay.rs:291`), so a record that used to match on a mix of precise and rounded values can now exit 1. The file is left as it was.

## Q7
Not executed: a real agy, muse or grok CLI for the bound-input rule; http `--rev` end to end; a no-hardlink crash on the claim; the `remove_file` race; HEAD moving between the two brief reads. The changelog's tests were not run. The README diff, the consult skill reference, and most test bodies were not read.

## Requested checks
RC1. In `crates/c3`, assert `agy_tool_step_is_writing` for `read_file` with `exec_path` = `rm -rf x` and with `research` = `git clean -fd`. Read-only. Both are false today (finding #1). One unit test.
RC2. Disposable repo: delete the live brief, differ HEAD from an older commit, run `--rev` of the older commit, compare the handoff brief sha256 with the worktree file. Workspace-write. They differ if HEAD's blob changes after the plan-time read (finding #2). 10 minutes.
RC3. Two no-hardlink placements of one patch name; pause between `file_state` and `remove_file`. Workspace-write. The finished sibling file is gone (finding #3). One fixture.

findings.claim: On an allow-listed agy reader, a command is not classified as writing when its key ends in a path/file/url/dir suffix or contains a search fragment such as search or glob, so a complete reply stays usable.
findings.trigger: A read_file (or other AGY_READ_ONLY_TOOLS) step logs parameters such as exec_path = rm -rf x, paths = [bash -c rm], research = git clean -fd, or global = rm -rf x, and the tree check then sees no writing step.

evidence.observation: Strings are command-scanned only for role Scanned. Write markers are tested first, then any key containing a search marker or ending in path/file/url/uri/dir/folder is Data and never scanned. research contains search; global contains glob.
An agy run with no writing step and a complete schema-valid reply is warned and the reply is kept even when the tree changed.

findings.remedy: Treat only known file-name parameters of each allow-listed reader as data. Scan every other key, and do not use substring matches such as glob inside global or search inside research.

findings.claim: The brief hash and the 'taken from revision HEAD' line are fixed at plan time, while staging reads the brief again and drift does not re-hash it, so the handoff and ledger can name bytes the reviewer did not read.
findings.trigger: The live brief is missing, committed_brief takes HEAD's blob, and before stage_bytes either the live file appears or HEAD's blob at that path changes. Under --rev the reviewed commit's own brief is skipped whenever HEAD has the path.

evidence.observation: committed_brief returns the string HEAD plus the blob read at plan time, and only then the reviewed revision.
Staging calls brief_bytes again, which returns a live file first and otherwise re-reads HEAD.
When brief_from_revision is set, brief_sha_after is the plan-time hash and brief_changed stays false.

findings.remedy: Hash the bytes staging actually wrote, name that commit sha rather than HEAD, and prefer the reviewed revision when --rev is set.

findings.claim: Claim cleanup removes the patch name after a stat, so a sibling's finished patch can be deleted, and a live owner stalled more than 60 seconds can later replace the file the other run published.
findings.trigger: No hard links. One placement's rename fails, or an empty claim is older than 60s, and the other placement's rename lands between file_state and remove_file. Or the first process resumes and renames onto the name after the takeover.

evidence.observation: drop_own_claim unlinks by leaf name once it has seen size 0 and the claim identity. It does not unlink the opened handle.
The 60s takeover uses the same stat-then-remove_file sequence and treats any unchanged empty file as abandoned, with no check that the owner has exited.
The owner's dir.rename runs after that window and, on a filesystem where rename replaces, writes its bytes over the name the other run already published.

findings.remedy: Unlink only the opened claim handle (or rename over the claim from the same directory handle without a separate delete). Take over a claim only when its owner pid is dead, not merely when the empty file is 60s old.

findings.claim: A live-tree reply is failed as a changed bound input when the brief or an artifact cannot be re-read, even if the bytes are unchanged.
findings.trigger: At the post-turn re-hash the brief path is locked or otherwise unreadable, or an artifact read fails. brief_sha_after becomes empty, or the artifact after-hash becomes missing.

evidence.observation: fs::read failure uses unwrap_or_default for the brief and unwrap_or_else missing for artifacts. Any difference from the pre-run hash sets brief_changed or artifacts_changed_paths.
A non-empty bound-changed list forces outcome failed and clears a usable reply.

findings.verification: Make the brief unreadable at the end of a fake live-tree consult (revoke read for the re-hash only) and read bridge_outcome.
findings.remedy: If the re-read fails, fail with 'could not be re-read' or retry. Do not report a content change unless two successful hashes differ.

findings.claim: An MCP consult or panel can pass diff and cannot pass --diff-tracked-only, so a one-revision diff from MCP always embeds untracked file content.
findings.trigger: c3_consult or c3_panel is called with diff set to one revision while the worktree has an untracked, not-ignored file.

evidence.observation: The forwarded string flags include diff and do not include diff_tracked_only.
The c3_consult input schema documents diff and has no tracked-only property. Panel and detach paths do thread the CLI flag.

findings.verification: Call the MCP consult tool schema and confirm diff_tracked_only is absent; run a one-revision diff through that builder and inspect the argv.
findings.remedy: Add a boolean diff_tracked_only to the MCP consult and panel schemas and append --diff-tracked-only when it is true.

findings.claim: When the pending stream's mtime is known and the noted stream's mtime is not, the death record keeps the pending path, which can be the older main stream.
findings.trigger: The status note names a continuation events file that bases.join cannot see as a file, while the pending record still names the main stream and that file's mtime is readable.

evidence.observation: The comment says the note wins when either time is unknown. The match returns false for (Some pending, None noted), so the pending path is kept.

findings.verification: Build a death record whose note path does not resolve under bases and whose pending path does, and compare events_file with the note.
findings.remedy: If the noted path does not resolve, keep the note when the pending file is the older name, or resolve both paths the same way the events file was stored.
